title: The Orbit of New Lagos
premise: Wren Thornbury has spent twelve years as the invisible caretaker of the abandoned Svalbard-adjacent seed vault, hauling cargo through orbits contested by two rival fleets. When a manifest lists a ship that never flew under a name Wren buried long ago, they discover their forged identity is the only thing keeping a fragile armistice alive: both fleets believe 'Wren Thornbury' is a neutral broker who died heroically decades ago. As the lie unravels and a young stowaway claiming to be the broker's heir forces Wren's hand, they must choose between preserving the peace built on a dead stranger or revealing themselves and risking war. In the end, Wren and the stowaway forge a new identity together—one that belongs to neither fleet but to the found family gathering around them—buying peace not with a lie, but with a promise.
about_author: Theo Nystrom is a former maritime logistics analyst who spent six years writing shipping manifests before turning them into science fiction. They live in a coastal town where the fog does most of the worldbuilding.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. During a routine cargo run through contested orbit, Wren discovers their own buried birth name on the manifest of the Meridian, a ship that never launched—listed as its captain. The emotional beat is dread: someone knows who Wren was before the vault, before the silence. A stowaway, Iyo, is found hiding in the hold carrying the same name.

chapters.title: The Broker Who Died Twice
chapters.summary: Iyo's POV. Iyo reveals they were raised on stories of the legendary neutral broker Wren Thornbury—their supposed grandparent—and sent to find the heir. Both fleets are converging on the vault for an inheritance ceremony that will decide control of the seed routes. Wren realizes their forged identity accidentally became the legend holding the armistice together. Beat: reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With the fleets arriving early, Wren impersonates the dead broker while Iyo plays the heir, improvising a ceremony neither understands. A fleet commander recognizes inconsistencies and threatens exposure; Wren's old contacts from the vault years surface as unexpected allies. Climax builds as the deception frays in real time. Beat: terror sharpening into fierce protectiveness of Iyo.

chapters.title: What We Leave Growing
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Exposed at the ceremony, Wren confesses the truth—but reframes it: the peace was never the broker's, it belonged to everyone who kept the routes open. Iyo publicly renounces sole inheritance, proposing shared stewardship of the vault among crews of both fleets. The fleets, weary of war, accept. Beat: grief for the old self dissolving into belonging—a family grown from a lie.
